THE WOMAN, VALENTINA TROFIMOVA MELNIKOVA, IS A MEMBER OF THE 
DISTRICT SOVIET (COUNCIL) AND CHAIRMAN OF ITS PERMANENT COMMITTEE 

ON CULTURE. A PROMINENT PARTY MEMBER, SHE IS ONE OF THOSE WHO HAVE 
BENEFITTED PERSONALLY FROM THE COMMUNIST REGIME. 

SHE SAID THE PEOPLE THROUGHOUT THE REGION WERE FREELY DISCUSSING 
KHRUSHCHEV'S SECRET SPEECH BEFORE THE COMMUNIST. PARTY CONGRESS 
DENOUNCING STALIN. SHE ADDED: THE INHABITANTS HAD NOTICED "THERE 
USED TO BE THE SAME SORT OF THING IN THE FACTORIES--THE CULT OF 
PERSONALITY, I MEAN. NOW THERE HAS BEEN A NOTICEABLE INCREASE OF 
CRITICISM FROM BELOW, ESPECIALLY PRACTICAL CRITICISM OF MINISTERS AND 

BUT WHEN THIS CONVERSATION WAS RESUMED OVER LUNCH, IN VERY FRANK 
DETAIL, IT APPEARED THAT THE FARM WOMEN WHO HAD PREPARED A LAVISH MEAL 
FOR THE VISITORS BY NO MEANS SHARED SUCH A SOPHISTICATED ATTITUDE. 

THEY WERE SHOCKED TO THE CORE BY WHAT WERE STARTLING REVELATIONS 
TO THEM AS WESTERN GUESTS AND THEIR HOSTS DISSECTED SECTIONS OF THE 
KHRUSHCHEV SPEECH. 

DRESSED IN THEIR HOLIDAY BEST, THEY CROWDED AROUND THE DINING 
ROOM DOOR IN THE SMALL NEW COUNTRY COTTAGE, DRINKING IT ALL IN. 

MRS. MELNIKOVA SAID THE SOVIET PRESIDIUM'S DECREE DRASTICALLY 
REDUCING CORRECTIVE LABOR CAMPS ALREADY HAD BEEN APPLIED WIDELY IN 
THIS AREA. IN FACT, SHE ADDED, THERE HAD BEEN A SPECIAL LOCAL 
DECREE ABOLISHING THEM. 

PYOTR MOSKOV, CHAIRMAN OF THE NOVOSIBIRSK CITY SOVIET, TOLD 
THIS REPORTER THAT A NEW "CITY CONSTRUCTION AUTHORITY® HAD TAKEN OVER 
BUILDING PROJECTS. HE INSISTED THERE NEVER WERE MORE THAN 1,000 
PERSONS IN THE SO-CALLED ®SPECIAL CONTINGENTS® WHICH HAD BEEN 
WORKING HERE. ,

UNDERSTAND WHY, ® AS SHE 8TRESSED THE ADVANTAGES OF THE NEW SYSTEM

THE UNITED STATES HAS NO DIPLOMATIC RELATIONS WITH EAST GERMANY 
AND UeSe BUSINESSMEN IN THE PAST HAVE STEERED CLEAR OF BECOMING OFFICIAL 
EXHIBITORS AT THIS MOSTLY WIDELY KNOWN FAIR BEHIND THE IRON CURTAIN. 
THE 1956 FAIR OPENED YESTERDAY. 

IT TOOK DETECTIVE WORK TO TRACK DOWN THE TINY STALL OF THIS 
EXHIBIT AMONG THOSE OF ABOUT 7,000 COMPANIES FROM 33 COUNTRIES ON 
BOTH SIDES OF THE IRON CURTAIN WHICH ARE PUTTING ON A RICH DISPLAY OF 
THEIR CONSUMER GOODS. 

WATCHED OVER BY AN EAST GERMAN WHO DESCRIBES HIMSELF AS A PRIVATE 
BUSINESSMAN, THE EXHIBIT FEATURES SEVERAL SMALL PILES OF SOMEWHAT 
BATTERED ORANGES, LEMONS AND GRAPEFRUIT ADVERTISED AS CALIFORNIA 
FRUIT. STAKED AROUND THE FRUIT ARE SEVERAL DOZEN CANS OF VEGETABLES, 
JUICES AND PRESERVED FRUIT. 

THIS EXHIBIT SHARES ONE OF THE SMALLEST CUBICLES IN THE 19 FAIR 
BUILDINGS WITH A FIRM DISPLAYING JAMAICAN BANANAS AND RUM. OVER THE 
ENTRANCE HANG AMERICAN AND JAMAICAN FLAGS. :

BY MILTON MARMOR 
-SCOTLAND YARD DROPPED ITS HUNT TODAY FOR 

NI} ONOMAL WOMAN CHAMPION DISCUS THROWERe THERE WAS 
GROWING SPECULATION THAT IT WAS ANOTHER STEP IN LETTERING HER BEAT THE 
RAP ON A CHARGE OF STEALING FIVE CHEAP HATS.» 

NINA WAS SAFE IN THE DIPLOMATIC TERRITORY OF THE SOVIET EMBASSY 
WHERE BRITISH LAW OFFICERS MAY NOT PENETRATE. 

BUT THERE WAS THE PROBLEM OF WHAT WOULD HAPPEN TO HER WHEN SHE 
LEFT THE EMBASSY IN AN ATTEMPT TO GET BACK HOME. 

THE CASE BALLOONED QUICKLY INTO AN INTERNATIONAL INCIDENT AND

, (AP) =POLICE ARRESTED THE SECRETARY OF THE 
CYPRUS Cheek ORTHODOX CHU! MARCHY TODAY AND ACCUSED HIM OF AIDING 
THE EOKA UNDERGROUND. THE ACTION SEEMED CERTAIN TO TOUCH OFF WIDESPREAD 
NEW RESENTMENT IN THE GREEK CYPRIOT COMMUNITY. 

GOVe SIR JOHN HARDING PERSONALLY ORDERED THE ARREST OF NICOS 
KRANIDIOTIS, A TALL, MILD-MANNERED INTELLECTUAL LEADER, AUTHOR AND 
POETs A GOVERNMENT STATEMENT SAID 

EVIDENCE NOW ACCUMULATED ON THE INITIAL ORGANIZATION AND PLANNING 
OF EOKA ESTABLISHES BEYOND A DOUBT THAT KRANIDIOTIS PLAYED A PROMINENT 
PART IN THE CONSPIRACY FROM ITS EARLIER DAYS." 

EOKA IS THE GREEK CYPRIOT UNDERGROUND THAT HAS WAGED A 16-MONTH 
CAMPAIGN OF VIOLENCE AGAINST BRITISH RULE AS PART OF THE MOVEMENT TO 
UNITE THIS ISLAND COLONY WITH GREECE. IT WAS BELIEVED KRANIDIOTIS' 
ARREST RESULTED FROM INFORMATION THE BRITISH SAY WAS FOUND IN RECENTLY 
CAPTURED EOKA DOCUMENTS.» 

BRITISH OFFICIALS CHARGED TWO WEEKS AGO THAT THE CAPTURED DOCUMENTS 
SHOWED EXILED ARCHBISHOP MAKARIOS, HEAD OF THE ETHNARCHY COUNCIL, PER- 
GONALLY DIRECTED THE EOKA CAMPAIGN. EOKA HAS DENOUNCED THE DOCUMENTS 


AS FORGERIES. 

KRANIDIOTIS, WHO IS IN HIS MIDDLE 40S, HAS OFTEN ACTED AS OFFICIAL 
SPOKESMAN FOR THE ETHNARCHY, WHICH EXERCISES SPIRITUAL LEADERSHIP OVER 
TIF 400,000 GREEK-SPEAKING RESIDENTS OF THE ISLAND. 

THE GOVERNMENT STATEMENT SAID KRANIDIOTIS WAS BEING QUESTIONED AND 
ADDED. "HE IS A DANGEROUS PERSON WHO SHOULD NOT BE LEFT AT LARGE." 

KRANIDIOTIS SPENT SEVERAL WEEKS IN LONDON IN JUNE, REPORTEDLY SEEKING 
SUPPORT IN BRITISH LABOR CIRCLES FOR CYPRIOT SELF-DETERMINATION. AT 
THAT TIME SEVERAL GREEK CYPRIOTS HERE ACCUSED HIM OF GOING BEHIND THE 
BACK OF THE ETHNARCHY, AND THE EXILED ARCHBISHOP, IN EFFORTS TO NEGO- 
TIATE A SETTLEMENT WITH THE BRITISH. 

ARCHBISHOP MAKARIOS CONDUCTED NEGOTIATIONS WITH THE BRITISH FOR 
CYPRUS INDEPENDENCE UNTIL APRIL, WHEN AUTHORITIES DEPORTED HIM TO THE 
SEYCHELLE ISLANDS IN THE INDIAN OCEAN FOR REFUSING TO CONDEMN EOKA VIO- 
LENCEs EVER SINCE, GREEK CYPRIOTS HAVE MAINTAINED THAT NEGOTIATIONS 
COULD BE RESUMED ONLY IF MAKARIOS IS RETURNED TO CYPRUS.

TO ISSUE A PASSPORT ALLOWING HIM TO TRAVEL ABROAD. 

SORESON APPEALED TO THE HIGH TRIBUNAL FROM A DECISION BY THE US. 
COURT OF APPEALS FOR THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA LAST JUNE 7. THE COURT 
OF APPEALS HELD THAT ROBESON HAD FAILED TO EXHAUST HIS ADMINISTRATIVE 
PEMEDIES BY NOT SEEKING A HEARING FROM PASSPORT OFFICIALS.« 

INSTEAD OF ASKING FOR A HEARING, ROBESON HAS CONTENDED THAT REGULA~ 
TIONS WHICH PROVIDE FOR ONE ARE INVALID. 

ROBESON, WHO HAS BEEN IDENTIFIED WITH COMMUNIST CAUSES OVER A 
NUMBER OF YEARS, HAS DECLINED TO SIGN A STATE DEPARTMENT AFFIDAVIT 
CANCEDNING PRFCENT OR PAST MEMBERSHIP IN THE COMMUNIST PARTY. 


NEGRO SINGER, TODAY APPEALED 
f DEPARTMENT 


~~ wet we aoe 


HIS APPEAL TO THE HICH TRIBUNAL SAID HE WAS RAISING THE QUESTION 
WHETHER THE STATE DEPARTMENT MAY LAWFULLY CONDITION THE ISSUANCE 
OF A PASSPORT TO AN AMERICAN CITIZEN "UPON THE APPLICANT'S COMPLIANCE 
WITH THE POLITICAL STANDARDS PROMULGATED BY THE DEPARTMENT." THIS 
QUESTION HAS NEVER BEEN DECIDED BY THE SUPREME 
COURT, THE SINGER SAID. 

THE APPEAL ADDED: 

"UNTIL THE LAST DECADE. THERE WERE NO GENERAL RESTRICTIONS UPON

TIONS OF AN AMERICAN CITIZENeee

LOUSs HE HAS BEEN THE VICTIM WITHIN THEUNITED STATES OF AN ECONOMIC

BY PREVENTING HIM FROM ACCEPTING LUCRATIVE SINGING AND ACTING ENGAGE- 
MENTS TO HIM ELSEWHERE IN THE WORLD." |

RABINOWITZ, OF NEW YORK CITY.

NEW ALGERIAN STATUTE HIS STAFF HAS BEEN DRAFTING IN PARIS. THERE WERE

WOULD FOLLOW, THEN ADMINISTRATIVE CHANGES WOULD BE DISCUSSED.

EUROPEANS PELTED MOLLET WITH TOMATOES AND CABBAGE ON HIS FIRST 
VISIT TO ALGIERS FEB. 6. BUT HIS SECOND VISIT PASSED ALMOST UNNOTICED. 
ONLY SOLDIERS, POLICE AND KNOTS OF NEWSMEN WERE ON HAND. 

MOLLET*S POLICIES SINCE FEBRUARY, PARTICULARLY HIS RECALL OF 
RESERVISTS FOR DUTY IN NORTH AFRICA, HAVE CONVINCED MOST EUROPEANS 
HERE MOLLET WILL NOT LET THEM BE SWALLOWED UP BY THE MOSLEM

AIR FORCES 
BY ELTON Cs FAY ¢. 

W )-THE TACTICAL AIR FORCE, WITH MORE UN 
AND PL ROAD THAN BASED AT HOME, IS PREPARING TO 
CHANGE THE BALANCE AND BUILD UP ITS CONTINENTAL STRENGTHe 

THIS MOVE IS THE LATEST IN THE TREND TO PLACE MORE AND MORE RELI- 
ANCE ON SWIFT MOBILITY AND THE RAPIDLY MOUNTING FIREPOWER OF NUCLEAR 
WEAPONS AND MISSILES. DECREASING MILITARY MANPOWER ALSO IS REFLECTED 
IN THE PROGRAMS. 

THE TACTICAL AIR FORCE OPERATES THE FLEETS OF JET FIGHTER-BOMBERS 
AND LIGHT BOMBERS, GUIDED MISSILES, THE AIRLIFT TRANSPORTS FOR 
GROUND FORCES AND TACTICAL RECONNAISSANCE. THE REDUCTION IN SIZE oF 
NUCLEAR WEAPONS, COMBINED WITH THE HIGH SPEEDS AND EXTENDED RANGES OF 
AIRCRAFT, HAS GIVEN THE TACTICAL AIR FORCE (TAC) STRIKING POWER 
APPROACHING THAT OF THE STRATEGIC AIR COMMAND (SAC). DURING THE Last 
TWO YEARS TAC HAS DEVELOPED AN AERIAL COMBAT-TRANSPORT PLANE SYSTEM 
WHICH PROVIDES IT WITH SWIFT GLOBAL MOBILITY. 

UNDER THE NEW PLAN TO BUILD UP THE BALANCE OF TACTICAL AIRPOWER AT 
HOME, TAC WILL USE ONLY PART OF A WING--A SQUADRON--TO SERVE WHERE 
THE EQUIVALENT OF A FULL WING HAS BEEN USED PREVIOUSLY, AN AIR FORCE 
SPOKESMAN EXPLAINED TODAY. 

_ THIS WILL BE WITHIN THE FRAMEWORK OF THE OVERALL "ROTATION" PLAN 
ADOPTED BY TAC AND SIMILAR TO THAT USED BY SAC. TAC UNITS, UNDER THIS 
PLAN, GO OVERSEAS FOR AN APPROXIMATE SIX-MONTH TOUR OF DUTY, THEN ARE 
REPLACED BY OTHER UNITS FROM THE UNITED STATES. 

GENe Oo Pe WEYLAND, CHIEF OF THE TACTICAL COMMAND, SAYS THE 
OVERALL STRENGTH OF THE FORCE--NOW ABOUT 46 WINGS, WITH A PLANNED 
BUILDUP TO ABOUT 50 BY A YEAR FROM NOW--WILL REMAIN THE SAME. UNDER 
GOlnHNENTAL UNITED staTES ULL BE INGREAGED BY ReDUTNC FoReES

SPECIAL MEANING.

F EGYPT AND TO START ARMED INTERVENTION," HE TOLD THE OPENING 
SESSION OF THE FIRST CHINESE COMMUNIST PARTY CONGRESS HELD IN 11 
YEARS. "WE MUST COMPLETELY FRUSTRATE THE SCHEMES OF IMPERIALISM To 
SREATE TENSION AND PREPARE FOR WAR."

SOLIDARITY WITH ALL PEACE-LOVING COUNTRIES.®

LOOK TO AGGRESSION FOR THEIR PROFITS.

COUNTRIES THERE HAS BEEN A TREND TOWARD RELAXATION OF TENSION IN 
THE INTERNATIONAL SITUATION.®

THEY WILL HAVE TO SHIFT FROM THEIR DAYS-ONLY WORKING STINT TO A 24-

ROUTE AROUND SOUTHERN AFRICA AS AN ALTERNATIVE TO THE SUEZ CANAL. 
THERE WAS A HINT THE SOUTH AFRICAN PORTS COULD NOT TAKE THE TRAFFIC, 

PORT CAPTAINS OF ALL SOUTH AFRICAN PORTS CONFERRED ON EMERCENCY 
PLANS AT TRANSPORT HEADQUARTERS AT JOHANNESBURG. : 

ARRANGEMENTS ARE BEING MADE TO OPERATE THROUGH THE NIGHT AND MOVE 
THREE TRANSIENT SHIPS THROUGH EACH BERTH EVERY 24 HOURS IF NECESSARY, 
BY STREAMLINING PORT AND BUNKERING FACILITIES. 

BUT TRANSPORT MINISTER BeJe SCHOEMAN HINTED FRIDAY, IN A SPEECH AT 
PORT ALFRED, THAT SOUTH AFRICA COULD NOT NOW COPE WITH THE 
DAILY TOTAL OF AT LEAST 40 SHIPS THAT PASS THROUGH 


SUEZ . 

AUTHORITIES HERE BELIEVE IT WOULD BE IMPOSSIBLE TO HANDLE MORE THAN 
20 EXTRA SHIPS ‘DAILY IN THE COUNTRY*'S FOUR MAJOR PORTS OF DURBAN, PORT 
ELIZABETH, EAST LONDON AND CAPETOWN. 

RECENTLY EIGHT MILLION POUNDS ($22 400,000) WERE EARMAKRED 
TO WIDEN THE TURNING BASIN IN EAST LONDON’S BUFFALO RIVER AND IMPROVE 
FACILITIES AT PORT ELIZABETH. BUT TO COPE ADEQUATELY WITH THE WORLD's 
TRAFFIC WOULD NEED AN IMMEDIATE EXPENDITURE OF MANY MILLIONS. 

WITH THE FIERCE WEATHER OF THE CAPE OF GOOD HOPE AT THE SOUTHERN 
POINT OF THE CONTINENT, IT IS NOT PRACTICAL TO REFUEL TRANSIENT SHIPS 
OUTISDE THE HARBOR IN THE ROADSTEAD OF TABLE BAY. DURING WORLD 
WAR II CONVOYS TRIED IT, USING TANKERS AS FLOATING FUEL STORES. BUT 
WITH THE CAPE ROLLERS AND SUDDEN FIERCE GALES OF THE POINT--ALSO CALLED 
THE "CAPE OF STORMS®,--THIS WAS A RISKEY WARTIME EXPEDIENT THAT PEACE— 
TIME SHIPWONERS WOULD BE UNLIKELY TO TRY. 

ONE FRIGHTENING INCIDENT OCCURRED IN 1940, WHEN THE BRITISH LINER - 
QUEEN MARY, TOO BIG FOR THE BERTHS, WAS inc 
THOUSANDS OF TONS OF FUEL OIL FROM’A TANKER. THE TIDE SWUNG 
THE SHIP*S BEAM ONTO THE CAPE'S FAMOUS GROUND SWELL. THE LINER AND ITs 
TANKER CONSORT ROLLED INTO EACH OTHER WITH A THUNDEROUS CLANG. 

IF THE SITUATION BECAME SUFFICIENTLY URGENT, HOWEVER 
EMERGENCY MEASUREES COULD BE TAKEN. THEMOST LIKELY WOULD BE TO SERVICE

LEMPLOYED IN THE BUILDING OF THE MID-CANADA LINE ARE ABOUT 3,500 
MEN. INCLUDING 294 INDIANS AND 59 ESKIMOS. 

{ANGUAGE PROBLEMS EXIST. SIGNS AT SOME CONSTRUCTION ASSEMBLY 
POINTS CARRY INDIAN AND ESKIMO CHARACTERSs

WHEN THE DECISION TO BUILD A MID-CANADA LINE WAS MADE IN 1953, 

MAPS OF MUCH OF THE AREA EITHER WERE NON-EXISTENT OR SKETCHY AND 
INACCURATE. THE RCAF, USING AERIAL PHOTOGRAPHY, AND LAND SURVEY 
PARTIES, COMPILED HIGHLY DETAILED TOPOGRAPHIC CHARTS OF THE WHOLE 
2.700-MILE STRIP.» 

‘ BUILDING DESIGN FOR ALL MID-CANADA LINE STATIONS IS_STANDARD.» 
ERECTED FROM PRE-FABRICATED MATERIAL, THE BUILDINGS ARE PAINTED IN 
CREAMS AND GREEN TO BLEND INTO THE LANDSCAPE AND REDUCE VISIBILITY. 
LIVING QUARTERS FOR THE OPERATING PERSONNEL ARE LOCATED IN BUILDINGS 
WHICH ALSO HOUSE EQUIPMENT AT THE INTERMEDIATE STATIONS. MAIN 
STATIONS ARE COMPLEXES OF BUILDINGS. 

ULTIMATELY, THE LINE WILL BE OPERATED BY ABOUT 800 CIVILIANS, 
WITH A SMALL NUMBER OF MILITARY OFFICERS AS SUPERVISORS. 

AT LEAST IN THE BEGINNING, THERE WILL BE NO WIVES OR FAMILIES 
LIVING ON THE MID-CANADA LINE. THE GOVERNMENT SAYS IT WILL "REVIEW 
THE REQUIREMENT FOR MARRIED QUARTERS AT A LATER DATE WHEN THE BIG 
WORKLOAD OF BUILDING THE LINE HAS BEEN COMPLETED."

POOLE SAYS THE ELECTRONIC EQUIPMENT OF MCL WILL BE "MUCH MORE 
ECONOMICAL THAN THE SCANNING RADAR ON DEWLINE AND PINETREE,*® BUT AT THE 
SAME TIME “WILL BE THE MOST ADVANCED EQUIPMENT POSSIBLE." 

A SUBSTANTIAL PART OF MCL WILL OPERATE AUTOMATICALLY AND UNATT- 
ENDED EXCEPT FOR OCCASIONAL INSPECTION AND MAINTENANCE VISITS FROM 
ADJACENT MAIN STATIONS. INTRICATE TELL-TALE SYSTEMS ARE BUILT IN TO 
INDICATE IMMEDIATELY BY BELL AND RED LIGHT WHEN ANY PIECE OF MACH- 
INERY AT AN UNMANNED STATION FAILS. FOR THE FIRST MONTHS OF 
ah a HOWEVER, BELL COMPANY TECHNICIANS WILL MAN ALL STATIONS TO 


CHECK ON EQUIPMENT. 
LATER, TEAMS OF CIVILIANS, WITH TWO OR THREE MILITARY PERSONNEL TO 
3 STATION OF THE LINE. 


SUPERVISE, WILL MAN EACH MAIN 

THE INTERMEDIATE STATIONS WILL TRANSMIT DATA BY SEVERAL RADIO 
CHANNELS TO THE MAIN STATIONS. FROM THOSE POINTS THE WARNING INFOR- 
INCLUDING THE AIR DEFENSE COMMAND AT COLORADO SPRINGS. Oy 

THE MANNER IN WHICH MCL GIVES WARNING WILL BE SOMETHING LESS THAN 
DRAMATIC, WITHOUT CLANGING BELLS, SIRENS OR WHISTLES. 

THE PRESENCE OF AN AIRBORNE ENEMY WILL BE SHOWN ONLY AS A VARIATION 
IN A LINE TRACED AUTOMATICALLY WITH A PEN RECORDING ON A ROLL OF GRAPH 
PAPER -- MUCH LIKE THE SEISMOGRAPH WHICH RECORDS EARTHQUAKES OR THE 
METEOROLOGICAL INSTRUMENTS USED BY WEATHER MEN. 

MODERN BOMBERS OF THE UNITED STATES AND PRESUMABLY OTHER MAJOR 
POWERS ARE EQUIPPED WITH GADGETS INTENDED TO "JAM® OR CONFUSE WARNING 


RADAR SYSTEMS. 

RCAF OFFICIALS SAY, WITHOUT TECHNICAL ELABORATION, THAT "NO 
RESPONSIBLE ORGANIZATION TODAY WOULD DEVELOP ANY ELECTRONIC DEVICE 
FOR DEFENSE WITHOUT TAKING INTO CONSIDERATION THE POSSIBILITY IT 
COULD BE JAMMED, AND TAKING SUCH DESIGN STEPS AS ARE NECESSARY TO 
REDUCE THE EFFECTS.® THE OFFICIALS ALSO SAY THAT “SPECIAL MEASURES* 
HAVE BEEN TAKEN TO GUARD AGAINST SABOTAGE OF UNMANNED STATIONS. 
NEWSMEN NOTICED THAT HIGH MESH WIRE FENCES, SURMOUNTED BY BARB 
WIRE, ENCLOSE INTERMEDIATE STATIONS.»

TO : POOL THEIR ATOMIC PATENT RIGHTS FOR 
PRIVATE NUCLEAR ENTERPRISES. 


EACH GOVERNMENT ASSIGNS TO THE OTHERS THE RIGHTS, TITLE AND INTERESTS 
IT OWNS IN THE OTHER COUNTRIES. LICENSE RIGHTS ARE FIRMLY HELD, 
HOWEVER, FOR MUTUAL DEFENSE PURPOSES.~ 

A NON-DISCRIMINATION CLAUSE BINDS EACH GOVERNMENT TO LICENSE 
NATIONALS OF THE OTHERS ON THE SAME TERMS ACCORDED ITS OWN NATIONALS. 

ATOMIC INVENTIONS AND DISCOVERIES COVERED BY GOVERNMENT-OWNED 
PATENTS AS OF LAST NOVe15 ARE AFFECTEDe THIS CUTOFF DATE INCLUDES 
THE TIME WHEN ATOMIC OPERATIONS WERE LARGELY A GOVERNMENT MONOPOLY IN 
THE UNITED STATES, BRITAIN AND CANADA 

A STATE DEPARTMENT COMMENT ON THE AGREEMENT SAID: 

"THE AGREEMENT IS EXPECTED TO BE OF PARTICULAR BENEFIT TO THE 
GROWING PRIVATE ATOMIC ENERGY IN EACH OF THE SIGNATORY COUNTRIES BY 
ELIMINATING QUESTIONS OF PATENT INFRINCEMENT.® 

THIS MEANS FIRMS WILL NEED LICENSES ONLY FROM THEIR OWN GOVERNMENTS. 
THE UNITED STATES, FOR EXAMPLE, COULD GRANT AMERICAN INDUSTRY ROYALTY- 
FREE LICENSES TO USE INVENTIONS DEVELOPED IN CANADA AND BRITAIN. 

THE ATOMIC DATA THUS MADE AVAILABLE IS OF TWO KINDS: 

te INVENTIONS ARISING FROM WARTIME COLLABORATION AMONG THE UNITED 
STATES, BRITAIN AND CANADA. RIGHTS TO THESE WERE ASSIGNED BY INVENTORS 
TO THEIR INDIVIDUAL GOVERNMENTS. | 

2. INVENTIONS DEVELOPED INDEPENDENTLY AND OWNED BY ONE OF THE 
THREE GOVERNMENTS. 

OFFICIALS SAID THERE ARE ABOUT 50 NUCLEAR INVENTIONS DEVELOPED 
DURING THE WARe THOSE ACQUIRED INDEPENDENTLY NUMBER SEVERAL HUNDRED. 
MANY OF BOTH KINDS ARE CLASSIFIED AS NATIONAL SECRETS, ANOTHER FACTOR 
LIMITING THE ISSUANCE OF PATENTS.

THAT'S A PHRASE TO COVER THE AID THE UNITED STATES GIVES A COUNTRY TO 
REPLACE FUNDS THAT COUNTRY USES TO BUILD UP ITS NATIONAL DEFENSE.

2e ALL OF THE 110 MILLIONS SENT EUROPE FOR NONMILITARY AID IN

3e THE BIGGEST SHARE OF THE NEARLY 2 1/2 BILLIONS SET ASIDE FOR 
THE WHOLE MUTUAL SECURITY PROGRAM DURING FISCAL 1956 WENT FOR DIRECT 
MILITARY AID AND DEFENSE SUPPORTe OF THE TOTAL, 843 MILLIONS WAS 
OBLIGATED OR RESERVED BY THE PENTAGON FOR DIRECT MILITARY ASSISTANCE. 

4. DURING JANUARY-JUNE 1956, THE UNITED STATES SHIPPED NEARLY TWO 
BILLION DOLLARS IN MILITARY GO6DS TO THE FREE WORLD. TWO-THIRDS OF

WASHINGTON, SEPT, 25 (AP)=THE WOR D BANK TODAY ANNOUNCED IT HAS 
ARRANGED TO SELL A 73 MILLION DOLLAR ISSUE OF TWO-YEAR BONDS TO 


INVESTORS OUTSIDE THE UNITED STATES. 
PRESIDENT EUGENE R. BLACK, ADDRESSING THE ANNUAL MEETING OF THE 
BANK'S BOARD OF GOVERNORS MERE, SAID THE SECURITIES, PAYABLE IN U, $, 

DOLLARS, HAS BEEN SUBSCRIBED BY INVESTORS IN 22 COUNTRIES, 

THE BONDS WILL PAY INTEREST AT 3 1/2 PER CENT A YEAR, PAYABLE 
SEMI*ANNUALLY STARTING NEXT APRIL 1. THE ISSUE IS DATED OCT. 1 
AND WILL MATURE OCT. 1, 3958, 

MUCK OF THE NEW IS 1g peinc TAKEN BY INVESTORS VHO HOLD TH 
BULK OF A 3 PER CENT, THREE-YEAR ISSUE WHICH MATURES OCT. 1, MANY’ 
OF THESE INVESTORS ASKED THE BANK TO PROVIDE AN OPPORTUNITY FOR THEM 
TO REINVEST THE PROCEEDS OF THE MATURING ISSUES. 

THE WEV ISSUE WILL BRING THE TOTAL OF OUTSTANDING WORLD BANK 
PONDS TO $50 MILLION DOLLARS=-¢93 MILLION OF U. $. DOLLAR BONDS AND 
THE EQUIVALENT OF 155 MILLION DOLLARS IN BRITISH STERLING, CANADIAN 
DOLLAR, SWISS FRANC AND NETHERLAND GUILDER BONDS.

BDEL HADI MADE HIS FLIGHT TO BAGHDAD FROM JORDAN AFTER LAST

ABDEL HADI IS SCHEDULED TO MEET IRAQI KING FAISAL TOMORROW WITH A 
MESSAGE FROM JORDAN’S KING HUSSEIN ON THE ISRAELI ATTACKS. THE Two 
21-YEAR-OLD KINGS ARE COUSINS IN THE HASHEMITE DYNASTY. 

FOR SEVERAL WEEKS THE IRAQIS HAVE BEEN PREPARING FOR A POSSIBLE 
MILITARY MOVE, AT JORDAN'S REQUEST. KING HUSSEIN VISITED BAGHDAD 
SEPT. 14 TO ASK IRAQ FOR AID--AFTER SEVERAL ISRAELI BORDER CLAS#S-~ 
UNDER THE TERMS OF THE TRAG- JORDAN TREATY OF 1947¢ AT THAT TIME 
IRAQI OFFICIALS PROMISED KING HUSSEIN THAT IRAQ WAS READY FOR MI{Itary 
ACTION AT ANY TIME. 

IN RESPONSE TO JORDAN APPEALS, THE IRAQIS BEGAN STOCKPILING 
MILITARY SUPPLIES AND MASSING TROOPS ALONG JORDAN'S FRONTIER TO BE 
READY TO MOVE AS THE SITUATION DEMANDED. 

UNDER THE IRAQ-JORDAN TREATY EITHER MAY ASK THE OTHER TO SEND 
TROOPS INTO ITS TERRITORY IN CASE OF NEFD. 

AT THE MOMENT, “IRAQ APPEARS TO BE THE ONLY ARAB NATION READY TO 
GIVE IMMEDIATE DIRECT MILITARY AID TO JORDAN. LAST WEEK EGYPT SENT ARMS

BY JOHN RODERICK (200) 


HONG KONG. SEP LaP=@-CHINESE COMMUNISTS TODAY’ ADOPTED A NEW 
PARES CONST EMT Payee 2 UP POWERFUL CONTROL COMMISSIONS TO DIscI- 
PLINE WAYWARD MEMDERS. 

THE CONTROL COMMISSIONS ARE ESTABLISHED WITHIN THE ENTIRE 
HIERARCHY, FROM COUNTY COMMITTEES TO THE RULING CENTRAL COMMITTEE. 

PEIPING RADIO SAID THEIR TASKS WILL BE TO "DEAL REGULARLY WITH 
VIOLATIONS OF THE PARTY CONSTITUTION, PARTY DISCIPLINE, COMMUNIST 
ETHICS AND THE STATE LAWS AND DECREE&amp;.«.TO DECIDE ON OR CANCEL 
DISCIPLINARY MEASURES AGAINST PARTY MEMBERS AND TO DEAL WITH APPEALS 
AND COMPLAINTS FROM PARTY MEMBERS." 

THEIR POWERS APPEAR TO EXTEND TQ THE HIGHEST MEMBERS OF THE 
CENTRAL COMMITTEE. 

THE CONSTITUTION'S 60 ARTICLE AND 9 CHAPTERS WERE ADOPTED 
UNANIMOUSLY AT THE EIGHTH PARTY CONGRESS IN PEIPING. 

ONE OF ITS ARCHITECTS, TENG HSIAO-PING, DESCRIBED IT AS "A 
POWERFUL INSTRUMENT BY MEANS OF WHICH WE SHALL FURTHER RAISE THE 
QUALITY OF THE PARTY, BROADEN THE SCOPE OF THE INNER PARTY DEMOCRACY, 
BRING INTO FULL PLAY THE POLITICAL ACTIVITY OF THE PARTY MEMBERSHIP, 
IMPROVE THE PARTY'S ORGANIZATION WORK AND STRENGTHEN ITS SOLIDARITY 
AND UNITY AND ITS FIGHTING CAPACITY." 

IN AN APPARENT MOVE TO PREVENT THE ERRORS OF ONE-MAN RULE AS 
EXEMPLIFIED BY THE STALIN ERA, THE CONSTITUTION STIPULATES THAT WHEN 
THERE ARE THREE OR MORE PARTY MEMBERS HOLDING RESPONSIBLE POSTS IN 
A GOVERNMENT OR PEOPLE'S ORGANIZATION, THEY WILL BE FORMED INTO A 

THEIR JOB WILL BE "TO ASSUME THE RESPONSIBILITY FOR CARRYING OUT 
PARTY POLICY AND DECISIONS, TO FORTIFY UNITY WITH NON-PARTY CADRES, 
TO CEMENT THE TIES WITH THE MASSES, TO STRENGTHEN PARTY AND STATE 
DISCIPLINE AND TO COMBAT BUREAUCRACY."

ONDONs SEPTe 29 (AP) “FIFTEEN OF THE 18 NATIONS WHICH HAVE 
ADVOCATED INTERNATIONAL CONTROL OF SUEZ INDICATED TODAY THEY WILL JOIN 
FORMALLY NEXT WEEK IN LAUNCHING THESUEZ CANAL USERS ASSN. (SCUA). 

THIS PROSPECT WAS DISCLOSED BY THEIR DIPLOMATIC REPRESENTATIVES IN 

ONDON. 
ONTHREE NATIONS HAVE EXPRESSED RESERVE ABOUT THE ASSOCIATION. 

JAPAN DECIDED TODAY TO PARTICIPATE IN THE SCUA CONFERENCE HERE 
OCTs 1 BUT DID NOT COMMIT ITSELF TO JOIN THE NEW BODY. 

PAKISTAN AND ETHIOPIA ARE STILL TO BE HEARD FROM. 

SCUA IS TO BE LAUNCHED AT A MEETING BEGINNING MONDAY IN STATELY 
LANCASTER HOUSE. IT WILL BE LONDON'S THIRD CONFERENCE ON SUEZ MATTERS 
SINCE EGYPTIAN PRESIDENT NASSER TOOK OVER THE CANAL JULY 26. 

BRITISH FOREIGN SECRETARY SELWYN LLOYD WILL OPEN THE MEETING, MADE 
uP OF AMBASSADORS, BEFORE FLYING OFF TO NEW YORK FOR THE U.N. SECURITY 
COUNCIL DEBATE ON THE SUEZ CRISIS. 

PREVIOUSLY HESITANT COUNTRIES WHICH HAVE DECIDED TO COME INTO 
SCUA ARE SWEDEN, DENMARK, TURKEY, IRAN AND SPAIN. 

THER MEMBERS WILL BE THE UNITED STATES, BRITAIN AND FRANCE--WHO 
SPONSORED THE PROJECT--AUSTRALIA, NEW ZEALAND, ITALY, PORTUGAL, NORWAY, 
THE NETHERLANDS AND WEST GERMANY. 

NOT ALL OF THESE COUNTRIES HAVE FORMALLY ADVISED THE BRITISH 
FOREIGN OFFICE THAT THEY WILL BE REPRESENTED IN MONDAY'S TALKS, BUT 
THEY ARE EXPECTED TO DO SO WITHIN THE NEXT 48 HOURS. 

SCUA IS INTENDED TO ENABLE CANAL USERS UNITEDLY TO PUSH THEIR 
CAMPAIGN FOR MULTI-NATION CONTROL OF SUEZ. 

PENDING A SETTLEMENT IT WILL SEEK DAY-TO-DAY WORKING ARRANGEMENT 
JITH EGYPT TO INSURE CONTINUED OPEN PASSAGE AND FIGURE WAYS OF 
ESSENING THE DEPENDENCE OF MEMBER NATIONS ON THE CANALe 

THE LONDON CONFERENCE WILL FORM AN EXECUTIVE COUNCIL 
REPRESENTING ALL MEMBER COUNTRIES, A SMALLER GOVERNING BOARD AND A 
SECRETARIAT WITH HEADQUARTERS PROBABLY IN ROME.

Ne StPle 28 CAP)-THE JUSTICE DEPARTMENT SAID TODAY IT HAS 
NOW OUS REASON TO DOUBT” THE TRUTHFULNESS OF ONE OF ITS

ACCORDINGLY, IN AN UNUSUAL MOVE, IT ASKED THE SUPREME COURT TO 
RETURN THE WHOLE CASE TO THE FEDERAL DISTRICT COURT AT PITTSBURGH TO 
DETERMINE WHETHER THE TESTIMONY GIVEN THE LOWER COURT BY JOSEPH D. 
MAZZEI WAS » IN FACT, THE TRUTH. ile 

MAZZEI WAS A GOVERNMENT INFORMANT, REPORTING TO THE FBI, ON COMMUNIST 
ACTIVITY IN WESTERN PENNSYLVANIA. 

HE TESTIFIED IN MARCH 1953 IN THE TRIAL OF STEVEN NELSON, WILLIAM 
ALBERTSON, BENJAMIN LOWELL CAREATHERS, JAMES HULSE DOLSEN AND IRVING 
WEISSMAN. THEY WERE CONVICTED THE FOLLOWING DECEMBER OF CONSPIRACY To 
TEACH AND ADVOCATE VIOLENT OVERTHROW OF THE GOVERNMENT. EACH WAS 
SENTENCED TO FIVE YEARS AND ALL ARE NOW FREE ON BOND. 

THE JUSTICE DEPARTMENT, IN ASKING THAT THE TRIAL BE REMANDED » SAID 
THAT IT STILL BELIEVES MAZZEI TOLD THE TRUTH IN THE PITTSBURGH TESTIMONY, 
BUT THAT HE HAS MADE SWORN STATEMENTS SINCE THEN~~IN OTHER PROCEEDINGS 
=--WHICH ARE NOT SUPPORTED BY EVIDENCE IN THE GOVERNMENT'S POSSESSION. 

THE DEPARTMENT ALSO SAID THAT MAZZEI'S PITTSBURGH TESTIMONY DIRECTLY 
INVOLVED ONLY CAREATHERS AND DOLSEN, AND HE WAS NOT PUT ON 
THE STAND UNTIL HIS TESTIMONY HAD BEEN CHECKED AND CORROBORATED AS 


FAR AS POSSIBLE. f 

BUT, IT SAID, THINGS THAT MAZZEI HAS SWORN TO SINCE HAVE RAISED 
SERIOUS DOUBT AS TO HIS VERACITY. : 

THE SUPREME COURT HAS TENTATIVELY SCHEDULED ARGUMENT THE WEEK OF 
8 ON THE APPEAL OF THE FIVE CONVICTED MEN. 

THE JUSTICE DEPARTMENT SAID ITS OFFICIALS HAD JUST LEARNED OF THE 
QUESTIONED POST-TRIAL STATEMENTS BY MAZZEI AND IT WAS ASKING AT THIS 
LATE STAGE THAT THE PITTSBURGH CASE BE REMANDED "BECAUSE WE FEEL 
COMPELLED TO DO SO BY OUR DUTIES."

(ADVANCE) SUEZ EGYPT. S P)-SAILING THROUGH 
IS ABOUT AS EXT ASA RIDE ON NEW YORK'S SIXTH AVENUE SUBWAY. 

FOR LONG STRETCHES THE VIEW FROM A SHIP, EXCEPT FOR THE NARROW 
STRIP OF WATER AHEAD AND BEHIND, IS JUST SAND. 

THE CANAL, CONCEIVED AND BUILT BY A FRENCHMAN WHO IS STILL HONORED 
HERE--FERDINAND DE LESSEPS--IS ROUGHLY BETWEEN 240 AND 300 FEES FROM 
BANK TO BANK EXCEPT WHERE IT PASSES THROUGH LAKE TIMSAH AT ISMAILTA 
AND FARTHER SOUTH THROUGH THE BITTER LAKES, ONE OF THE SALTIEST BODIES 
OF WATER IN THE WORLD. 

THE MAIN CHANNEL, MARKED BY BUOYS IS 180 TO 240 FEET WIDF. 
DOESN'T GIVE A BIG SHIP MUCH ROOM FOR MANEUVER. 

WHICH ARE THE MAIN CUSTOMERS ARE GETTING BIGGER AND BIGGER. 

THIS CORRESPONDENT WENT WITH A CONVOY OF NINE SHIPS, FORMED IN port 
SAID HARBOR. EACH SHIP HAD A WEARY EGYPTIAN PILOT ON THE BRIDGE. 

MOST OF THEM HAD PILOTED SHIPS UP FROM SUEZ IN AN EARLIER CONVOY, 
THEY HAD SLEPT ABOUT FOUR HOURS BETWEEN CONVOYS.

BONN. GERMANY. SEPTe 29 (AP)&lt;“CHANCELLOR KONRAD ADENAUER AND ‘PREMIER 
GUY MOLLET OF FRANCE TONIGHT CONCLUDED A HISTORIC AGREEMENT TO RETURN 
THE RICH SAAR TO GERMANYs THEY HAILED THE ACCORD AS THE FIRST STEP 
TOWARD A EUROPEAN UNION. 

*CERMANY AND FRANCE ARE NOW PREPARED TO WALK HAND-IN-HAND IN 
WORKING FOR EUROPEAN INTEGRATION,® THE GERMAN CHANCELLOR TOLD 300 
NEWSMEN AT THE END OF 12 HOURS OF HARD BARGAINING.

AHEAD FASTER WITH EUROPEAN INTEGRATION. ®

IN 1945.

FEDERATION

OF THE CANAL IMPERILED EUROPEAN OIL RESOURCES AND °WE MUST HAVE ALL THE 
MEANS OF DEVELOPING OUR OWN FORM OF ENERGY.

ONE OWNER TO ANOTHER SINCE IT GAS FIRST CEDED TO FRANCE IN 1797, 
BEFORE THAT IT WAS DIVIDED AMONG THE PALATINE DUCHY OF SAAR- 
ZWEIBRUCKEN, THE COUNTY OF ZWEIBRUCKEN AND FRANCE. .. 
UNDER THE TREATY OF PARIS IN 1815, THE SOUTHEAST PART OF THE Saar 
PASSED TO THE BAVARIAN PALATINATE pe REST TO PRUSSIA. 
AFTER YORLD WAR Iy_THE VERSAILL EATY CREATED AN. 
AUTONOMOUS SAAR TERRITORY TO BE ADMINISTERED BY FRANCE UNDER LEAGur 
OF NATIONS SUPERVISION UNTIL THE PEOPLE COULD VOTE A PREFERENCE, 
THE POPULACE VOTED IN 1935 TO RETURN TO GERMANY, WHICH THEN 
ORGANIZED IT AS THE SAARLAND PROVINCE. :

WORLD WAR II AND GAVE IT OVER TO FRENCH MILITARY GOVERNMENT IN JuLy 
1945, THE PEOPLE VOTED OCT. 5, 1947 OVERWHELMINGLY FOR ECONOMIC

G RED HUNGARY JOINED PRESIDENT TITO AND NIKITA KHRUSHCHEV AT 
THEIR MYSTERIOUS YALTA CONFERENCE TODAY. 
A MOSCOW BROADCAST MADE IT APPEAR THE MEETING WAS ONLY A HAPPY 


FATHER GATHERING. BUT WESTERN DIPLOMATS ARE SURE THE MEETING IS CON- 
SERNED WITH DEEP CONFLICTS WITHIN THE SOVIET BLOC. : 
THE YUGOSLAV PRESIDENT IS BELIEVED PLAYING A KEY ROLE IN A COM- 
MUNIST BLOC STRUGGLE FOR POWER ERUPTING FROM THE DOWNGRADING OF STALIN 

AND SOFTER SOVIET TREATMENT OF ITS EAST EUROPEAN SATELLITES. 

IT WAS PRESUMED KHRUSHCHEV WOULD USE THE OCCASION TO TRY TO ERASE 
ONE SOURCE OF TROUBLE--THE FRICTION BETWEEN YUGOSLAVIA AND HUNGARY. 

GEROE'S RISE TO THE PREMIERSHIP IN HUNGARY LAST JULY WAS A SOP TO 
TITO.  GEROE DISPLACED’ MATYAS RAKOSI, A STALINIST WHO TOOK A LEADING 
ROLE IN OUSTING TITO FROM THE COMINFORM EIGHT YEARS AGO. 

GEROE ORDERED A LARGE-SCALE RELEASE OF TITOIST HUNGARIANS, WHOSE 
IMPRISONMENT WAS A MAIN SOURCE OF FRICTION WITH YUGOSLAVIA. THE TWO 
COUNTRIES STILL HAVE ECONOMIC SCORES TO SETTLE. | 

WESTERN DIPLOMATS BELIEVE KHRUSHCHEV IS CONCERNED, PRIMARILY, WITH 
GETTING TITO’S SUPPORT FOR HIS DE-STALINIZATION POLICY. 

REPORTS TO LONDON DIPLOMATS INDICATE KHRUSHCHEV IS LOCKED IN A 
STRUGGLE WITH OLD BOLSHEVIKS IN THE SOVIET HIERARCHY. 

FORMER FOREIGN MINISTER Ve Me MOLOTOV AND DEPUTY PREMIER LAZAR 
KAGANOVICH, TWO OLD STALINISTS, ARE SAID TO FEEL KHRUSHCHEV HAS GONE 
TOO FAR With HIS SOFTER APPROACH, WEAKENING THE SOVIET POSITION 

TITO IS SUPPOSED TO BE UNHAPPY ABOUT A LETTER SENT BY MOSCOW TO. 
SOVIET SATELLITES WARNING THEM AGAINST EMBRACING *TITOISM"=-THAT IS, 
HIS ASSERTED INDEPENDENCE OF MOSCOW--TOO WHOLEHEARTEDLY. THE LETTE 
ALSO SAID YUGOSLAV COMMUNISTS WERE NOT TRUE MARXIST~LENINISTS.

aS IDEOLOGICAL IN CHARACTER. THE SPOKESMAN ALSO SAID HE KNEW OF THE 
SOVIET LETTER TO THE SATELLITES BUT HAD NOT SEEN IT.

BEGAN TO NORMALIZE THEIR RELATIONS, THE SOVIET BLOC HAS SHOWERED 
ECONOMIC BENEFITS ON YUGOSLAVIA IN SUCH QUANTITY THAT YUGOSLAVS HAVE 
AT TIMES REFUSED SOME OF THEM. 

BY LAST APRIL, ACCORDING TO THE ESTIMATE OF AN AMERICAN GOVERNMENT 
ECONOMIC EXPERT, THESE BENEFITS--PARTLY IN THE FORM OF GRANTS BUT 
MOSTLY IN EASY @REDITS FOR INDUSTRIAL EQUIPMENT AND THE LIKE--AMOUNTED 
TO ABOUT 300 MILLION DOLLARS, —/y~7oseA rc O—

EQUIPMENT VALUED AT 175 MILLION DOLLARS. COMMUNIST HUNGARY, AT SOVIET 
URGING, AGREED TO PAY TITO 85 MILLION DOLLARS IN COMPENSATION FOR THE 
STALIN@INSPIRED BOYCOTT WHICH BEGAN IN 1948. 

OTHER SATELLITE AND SOVIET ECONOMIC AID HAS BEEN HEAPED ON THE PILE, 
ADDING UP TO A CONSIDERABLE SUM FOR A COUNTRY THE SIZE OF YUGOSLAVIA.

OF ABOUT 6 " ey

EGYPT. (FROM JULY TO OCTOBER THE BLUE NILE, RISING IN THE
